title: Can Iraq PM rein in Kataib Hezbollah without triggering armed conflict?
gist: More than 40 days after the US-led coalition's withdrawal from Iraq, PM Ali al-Zaidi cancelled Mosul airport service contracts of three firms over 'links to armed groups', prompting a Kataib Hezbollah media campaign against him and raising risk of armed conflict with Iran-backed factions.

insights.claim: More than 40 days after the US-led coalition withdrew from Iraq, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's government may be inching toward armed conflict with Iran-backed factions including Kataib Hezbollah.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Post-withdrawal Iraq faces intra-Shia security risk; watch for clashes affecting stability and oil operations.
insights.quote: may be inching closer to armed conflict with Iran-backed factions

insights.claim: On Nov. 7 Zaidi cancelled service contracts of Sky Plus, Sama al-Matar and Al-Faisal al-Shamikh at Mosul International Airport, citing 'links to armed groups', and directed they be offered to international companies.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Targeting militia economic networks is the government's lever; a test case for squeezing faction revenue.

insights.claim: Kataib Hezbollah and its political wing Harakat Huqooq responded with a media campaign accusing Zaidi over how he built his wealth and his alleged past support for Iran-based factions.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Militia pushback signals contested authority; escalation from media to force is the risk.
insights.locator: Kataib Hezbollah (KH), one of the Iran-backed militias
